title: India concludes WTO review on tariffs, FTAs and trade reforms
content:
India’s eighth Trade Policy Review has concluded at the WTO in Geneva, with 68 WTO Members intervening across two July sessions.
For textile and apparel exporters and importers, the review signals continued scrutiny of tariffs, customs, quality orders and trade remedies.
India said reforms, FTA strategy and customs simplification support a predictable trade and investment regime.

title: India's Trident Group Q1 profit rises 55% QoQ to $1.58 mn
content:
Indian home textiles company Trident Group reported a strong Q1FY27 performance, with consolidated income rising 9.3 per cent QoQ to ₹1,803 crore (~$18.03 million) and net profit increasing 55 per cent to ₹158 crore (~$1.58 million). 
Improved yarn prices, cost discipline, and operational efficiencies supported margin expansion. 
The company remains optimistic about export growth.

title: Can India unlock $7 bn in apparel exports without new capacity?
content:
India could add several billion dollars in garment exports by improving planning, utilisation and delivery, but the full $7 billion upside is not idle capacity.
TexPro data shows India’s selected-market apparel share barely moved from 2021 to 2025 as Bangladesh, Vietnam and Cambodia gained.
Exporters must first reverse 2026 declines, then build capability in sweaters, outerwear and MMF-rich

title: ICE cotton gains modestly, weak export demand limits rally
content:
ICE cotton futures extended gains for a fourth straight session, supported by stronger crude oil prices and broader strength in agricultural commodities.
However, weak US export sales, a firmer US dollar and light trading capped gains.
Traders continue to monitor weather, export demand, Brazil's larger crop outlook and China's reserve auctions.

title: Bangladesh labour reforms gain ILO backing amid LDC transition
content:
ILO chief Gilbert F Houngbo held high-level talks in Bangladesh on labour law reform, social dialogue, job creation and social protection.
The agenda matters for apparel exporters and factory operators tracking compliance in the ready-made garment sector.
Bangladesh’s labour complaint is set to return to the ILO Governing Body in March 2027.

title: Bangladesh doubles ERQ for goods, exporters relying heavily on imports
content:
Bangladesh Bank has doubled the exporters' retention quota for goods, exporters relying heavily on imported raw materials, intermediate goods, machinery and other production inputs, raising the permissible retention limit from 7.5 per cent to 15 per cent of the repatriated FOB value. 
The decision is expected to provide exporters with greater flexibility in managing their foreign currency requirements.
